The purpose is that this word, through its sound, its impact and its intensity, creates a reverberation in the atmosphere, which has a far-reaching allusion. Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 101, verse 6:

The meaning of the scales being heavy or light is that the measures which carry weight with Allah and the measures which carry no weight with Him are what is intended. This is what the overall manner of expression of the Holy Qur'an makes known. And Allah knows best!

As for the rational and verbal discussions which the exegetes (mufassirin) and theologians (mutakallimin) conduct concerning these matters, this is an injustice to the Holy Qur'an. It is only those people who are not acquainted with the true priorities and concerns of the Holy Qur'an who engage in such discussions.

Fa-amma man ................ mawazinuh (6:101): "Then as for him whose values are weighty" (Qur'an 101:6-7 context), "and with Allah they will be sound."

So he will be in a pleasing life (7:101) — "he will be in a life that pleases him," and the details of this life are left unspecified. That is, it will be a life with which he is content, for the best blessing is that a person is content with his state.
Then as for him ................ whose scales are light (8:101). According to Allah's standard and criterion.

The passage is a commentary on Surah 101 (al-Qari'ah), verse 9, which the Urdu text quotes as: فامه هاوية (101:9).

Translation of the passage:

"Then his mother will be the Abyss (Hawiyah)." Literally, a mother is the place of refuge of a child, so for such people their place of refuge will be the deep pit of Hell, and therefore it is their mother. What a beautiful manner of expression, which is fitting to the occasion and the context. Here the punishment has been kept general, so that in the following verse its explanation may be given in a manner that is very impactful.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 101, verse 10:

﴿Wa ma adraka ma hiyah﴾ (101:10): "And what will make you know what it is?" This is the well-known style of expression in the Holy Qur'an: to make something appear terrifying, it says, "What would make you know what it is?"

And then after this comes an answer, and that answer is the final blow.

Fire, blazing hot. (Qur'an 101:11) "It is a blazing fire."

And those whose scales are light and unreliable, the scorching fire will be their mother. They will rest in that mother's lap and find comfort there. Or have you understood what kind of rest they will find in that mother's lap, a deep pit with a scorching fire within it? This sudden sarcastic tone is so real and so bitter that it cannot be imagined.
